name: Compression framework (LZFSE)
baseline: Compression framework COMPRESSION_ZLIB (zlib level 5) and NSData.compressed(using: .zlib)
verdict_reason: Apple claims zlib-level ratio at 2x to 3x the speed. An independent lzbench run of the open-source LZFSE reference shows 3.4x faster compression and 2.3x faster decompression than zlib -6 at almost the same ratio.
tier_reason: Independent lzbench run with public code, CPU, compiler and corpus stated, matching Apple's first-party claim.
claimed_speedup: Apple: 2x to 3x faster for both encoding and decoding at zlib's ratio. lzbench: 91.1 MB/s vs 26.8 MB/s compression (3.4x) and 732 MB/s vs 314 MB/s decompression (2.3x) against zlib 1.3.2 -6, ratio 31.91% vs 32.19% (derived from page data)
workload: Silesia corpus (silesia.tar, 212 MB), single thread, whole-file compress and decompress
hardware: AMD EPYC 9555P at 3.20 GHz, turbo off, single thread
install: built into iOS 9+ / macOS 10.11+ (Compression framework; NSData.compressed(using: .lzfse) on iOS 13+ / macOS 10.15+)
one_liner: Apple's LZFSE matches zlib's ratio while compressing 3.4x and decompressing 2.3x faster in an independent benchmark.
how_it_is_fast: LZFSE pairs an LZ77 match finder with Finite State Entropy coding, a table-driven form of asymmetric numeral systems that decodes symbols with table lookups and shifts instead of Huffman bit-by-bit decoding. Its encoder is tuned for speed at a ratio near zlib level 5. Apple also describes it as more energy-efficient than zlib.
use_it_when: Data that is compressed and decompressed only on Apple devices
You want zlib's ratio with less CPU time and energy
Streaming is needed (unlike LZMESH, LZFSE works with the stream API)
skip_it_when: The other side is a server, browser or non-Apple client that expects gzip/zlib
Targeting iOS 27 / macOS 27 or later only: Apple now recommends LZMESH for new Apple-only code
caveats: lzbench measures the 2017 open-source LZFSE reference on x86 Linux, not the tuned build inside Apple's OS on Apple silicon
lzbench compares stock zlib -6; Apple's COMPRESSION_ZLIB is its own level-5 implementation with a decoder Apple optimized
Apple's 2x to 3x claim gives no data set or hardware
The lzbench author has contributed to zstd; he has no stake in LZFSE or zlib
tradeoffs: Format is effectively Apple-only; the reference decoder exists but is rarely installed elsewhere
Lower ratio than LZMA or zstd at higher levels

evidence.quote: while running 2x to 3x faster for both encoding and decoding
The tests were run on a single thread of an AMD EPYC 9555P processor at 3.20 GHz
It targets similar compression rates at higher compression and decompression speed compared to deflate using zlib.
